title: Skeleton refactor before parallel build: Gateway.tick() seam, tool dispatch interface, RNG module
outcome: Barrier is I/O+timing only behind Gateway.tick(); tools dispatch via a world/state interface; RNG lives in ks.rng — so owners don't collide
acceptance: gateway has no TOOLS table; dispatch via interface implemented by world
ks.world does not import ks.runtime; all tests green
summary: Done. (1) runtime/barrier.py is now I/O + timing only: it sends what Gateway.open(tick, agents) returns, collects frames with deadlines and signer I/O, calls Gateway.tick(tick, [InFrame]) -> [(conn_id, ReplyFrame)], then does the sends, the K-miss/oversize close and the witness push. Epoch/view, admission and dispatch, plus agent_id ordering, now live in the gateway. TickBarrier no longer takes epochs. (2) gateway/stub.py has no TOOLS table. The new ks.gateway.dispatch defines the ToolDispatcher protocol (classify(env)->ActionClass, execute(env, txn)->Execution(result, read_set, write_set); StateTxn placeholder, None until ks.state is wired), and the record now carries read/write sets from Execution. ks.world.tools.SkeletonDispatcher implements it, and run.py wires it in. Gateway(..., dispatcher=) is a required kwarg. (3) RNG moved to ks.rng; runtime/rng.py is deleted, and world/skeleton and agent_template import ks.rng. ks.world never imports ks.runtime. src/ks/ARCHITECTURE.md maps module -> owner -> interface. New tests/skeleton/test_boundaries.py (5 tests) checks the seams: barrier AST, no TOOLS, world imports, rng location, Gateway.tick ordering and dispatch. Behaviour unchanged: ks run (seed 7, 3 agents, 6 ticks) + ks verify --head gives OK and anchored, and the suite is 462 passed. ks.state was not touched. Note: running pytest at the same time as another ks run fails intermittently with K2 'processes already run under uids 60000..' because uids are shared on this machine; this is environmental and was there before.
